title: fig04 is synthetic because it reads v1 CSV names that were never produced -- the v2 tables exist with matching columns

claims.statement: fig04_omission_identity_decoding.py's Panels B/C/D fall to their hardcoded synthetic branches solely because of a filename mismatch: the script reads omission_identity_{timecourse_master,decoding_master,glmm_coefficients}.csv, while the producer scripts/compute_omission_identity_encoding_v2.py writes the same three tables with a _v2 suffix. All three _v2 files exist on disk and their headers match the columns the plotting script expects.
claims.receipt: fig04_omission_identity_decoding.py:146-149 (tc_csv/slot_csv/glmm_csv paths, no _v2); compute_omission_identity_encoding_v2.py:411-413 (to_csv with _v2); ls outputs/classification -> omission_identity_{decoding_master,timecourse_master,glmm_coefficients}_v2.csv, all dated 2026-08-06 21:47. Headers: timecourse [session,area,time_ms,accuracy,n_units,n_trials]; decoding [status,accuracy,...,area,slot_key,session,...]; glmm [session,unit_id,area,coefficient_beta,abs_beta,quality,note] -- every field the script indexes is present.

claims.statement: The fig04 README's highest-priority item 0 ('none of the three source CSVs exist on disk ... compute_omission_identity_encoding.py has apparently never been run to completion') is now factually wrong. It was written 2026-08-06 at promotion time, before the v2 run landed the same evening.

Wiring the _v2 tables in would invert the figure's message rather than confirm it. The placeholder encodes a monotonic frontal>occipital hierarchy peaking at FEF 0.78 / AUC 0.84; the real v2 slot table has an overall mean of 0.601 against a 0.5 chance baseline with V2 (0.711 at p2) highest and FEF (0.578) mid-pack -- no frontal gradient.
claims.receipt: outputs/classification/omission_identity_decoding_master_v2.csv, status==success, groupby(slot_key,area).accuracy.mean(): p2 V2 0.711, V4 0.630, PFC 0.622, V3 0.602, V1 0.579, FEF 0.578, TEO 0.571. Overall mean 0.601. vs fig04 script's hardcoded slot_summary p2 = FEF 0.78 ... V1 0.54 and E2's AUC 0.84/0.72.

claims.statement: The v2 tables' above-chance 0.601 is the confounded random-CV estimate. The leave-one-cycle-out, per-cycle mean-centered redesign run the same night lands at chance, so the v2 numbers must not be presented as a decoding result without that qualifier.
claims.receipt: outputs/classification/omission_identity_cycle_deconfound_p2.csv (147 rows, written 2026-08-06 22:09): mean acc_loco_meancentered = 0.495 vs the v2 master's 0.601 on the same corpus.

claims.statement: The permutation null that three separate 2026-08-07 nodes list as 'blocked_on / still running' has NOT landed at corpus scale. What exists on disk is a single-session, 5-permutation smoke run for spikes only; there is no LFP null file at all. A 5-permutation p-value is quantised to multiples of 1/6, which is why every reported p is 0.167/0.333/0.5/0.667.
claims.receipt: outputs/classification/fig04_v8_permnull_spikes.csv -- 15 lines total (14 data rows), all sub-C31o_ses-230816, n_perm=5 in every row, p_value in {0.1667,0.3333,0.5,0.6667}. No fig04_v8_permnull_lfp.csv exists. Written 2026-08-07 08:11, i.e. BEFORE the nam node (08:32) that describes it as still running.

claims.statement: The fig04 README's issue 4 ('possible band-definition drift', LFP_BANDS with gamma unsplit 30-80) resolves as dead code, not drift: LFP_BANDS is defined in jnwb/omission_identity.py and referenced nowhere, in that file or any other module or script.
claims.receipt: grep -n LFP_BANDS jnwb/*.py scripts/*.py -> single hit, jnwb/omission_identity.py:47 (the definition itself).

claims.statement: The p4 A/B label swap fix in OMISSION_IDENTITY_CONDITIONS postdates the v2 tables, so the p4 rows of all three _v2 CSVs carry the wrong ground-truth labels by the fix's own stated rule.
claims.receipt: jnwb/omission_identity.py mtime 2026-08-06 22:58 vs the three _v2 CSVs at 21:47; the fix comment itself states 'every p4-specific number computed before this fix ... must be treated as unreliable until rerun'.
claims.note: mtime shows only that the FILE was last edited after the run, not that the p4 hunk specifically was. Confirming needs the run's own provenance, which the v2 CSVs do not carry. Direction of the error is safe either way: rerun before quoting p4.

issues: Graph health, measured 2026-08-08 over 370 nodes: 1 dangling edge target ('fig04-identity-decoding', referenced by bilinear-2d-decoder-v7-20260807, no such node file); 2 duplicate edges; schema_version is absent on 199 of 370 nodes and appears in four spellings among the rest (3, '3.0', 'v14', 'v3'). No unparseable files.

6 lab nodes and 13 scripts plus jnwb/bilinear.py and jnwb/nam.py are untracked; the p4 label fix and 178 new lines in jnwb/omission_identity.py are uncommitted. The most current state of this analysis exists only in the working tree.

The PLACEHOLDER-DUMMY rule is working as intended -- fig04.svg does carry the red flag. The rule caught the symptom; it did not catch that the cause was a one-word path bug with the real data sitting next to it.
falsifier: Closed when fig04's three CSV paths are repointed to the _v2 files (or the producer is rerun to the v1 names), the figure is regenerated, and the PLACEHOLDER-DUMMY flag is either gone or still present for the E1/E2 panels only -- with the README's item 0 rewritten to match what is actually on disk.
